Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.

1. Heard counsel for the applicants and Sri V.P. Tripathi, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet no. 72 of 2021 dated 16.08.2021 as well as the summoning order dated 20.09.2021 and the entire proceedings of Case No. 27085 of 2021, CNR No. UPMO04010051 of 2021 (State vs. Lalit Kumar @ Monu and others)

sentences.text:
1 3 . Learned counsel for the applicants submits that:-
(i) the applicant no.2 is the father-in-law and the applicant no. 3 is the mother-in-law of the opposite party no. 2.

On 17.05.2022, the court passed the following order;
"Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A.
This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the charge sheet no. 72 of 2021 dated 16.8.2021 as well as entire proceeding of Case No. 27085 of 2021 including the cognizance as well as summoning order dated 20.09.2021 passed by Civil Judge (Jr. Div)/FTC (Crime Against Women), Moradabad arising out of Case Crime No. 135 of 2021 under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C.
and 3/4 D.P Act, P.S.- Mahila Thana, District- Moradabad with an alternative prayer to stay the further proceedings of the above mentioned case.

I have heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned AGA. and have gone through the materials available on record carefully and I do not find any substance in the arguments advanced by learned Counsel for the applicant.
The prayer to that extent on behalf of applicant no.1 namely, Lalit Kumar @ Monu (husband) is hereby refused.

However, if the applicant may move bail application before competent Court of Jurisdiction, the Court below shall decide the same as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law, considering all aspects of the matter.

So far as applicant no. 2 and 3 is concerned, it has been contended by learned counsel for the applicants that they are the family members of applicant no.1 and the allegation levelled against them are wholly vague and no specific allegation has been levelled against them.
Learned counsel for the applicants has placed reliance on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra vs. State of U.P. and others reported in 2012 (10) ADJ 464.

sentences.text:
Notice on behalf of opposite party no. 1 has been accepted by learned A.G.A.
Issue notice to opposite party no.2 returnable within three weeks at the address given in the application.
Opposite party no.2 may file counter affidavit within four weeks.
Learned A.G.A. may also file counter affidavit within the same period.
Rejoinder affidavit may thereafter be filed within two weeks.

Till the next date of listing, further proceedings of Case Crime No. 135 of 2021 under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P Act, P.S.- Mahila Thana, District- Moradabad in respect of applicant nos. 2 and 3 shall be kept in abeyance."

By order dated 24.02.2023, the present writ petition was connected with Application U/S 482 No.
6960 of 2023.

Today, following order was passed in the connected writ petition;
"1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard counsel for the applicant, Sri J.K. Sharma, counsel for the opposite party no.
2 and Sri V.P. Tripathi, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet no. 72 of 2021 dated 16.08.2021 as well as the summoning order dated 20.09.2021 and the entire proceedings of Case No. 27085 of 2021, CNR No. UPMO04010051 of 2021 (State vs. Lalit Kumar @ Monu and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 135 of 2021,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Moradabad, on the basis of compromise.

entities.text: State vs. Lalit Kumar @ Monu and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. It is stated that compromise deed had been filed by the parties before the trial court.

Further,
pursuant to the order dated 24.02.2023, the parties appeared before the court, duly identified by their counsels and the court verified the compromise vide order dated 02.03.2023 annexed as Annexure-S.A. no. 1 to the supplementary affidavit.
6.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.

Lalit Kumar @ Monu And 2 Others vs State Of U.P And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76019240/
3

entities.text: Lalit Kumar @ Monu And 2 Others vs State Of U.P And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.

8. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

9. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case, in respect of the applicant, are hereby set aside.

sentences.text: 10. The present application is, accordingly, allowed."
5. In view of the fact that the parties have entered into compromise and have settled their dispute amicably, the proceedings against the applicants are also liable to be set-aside.
6. In view, thereof, the proceedings of the aforesaid case, in respect of applicants, are set-aside.
7. The present application is, accordingly, allowed.
